questions.topic: Atomic structure and the periodic table
questions.q: An atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What are its mass number and atomic number?
options: Mass number 12 and atomic number 11
Mass number 23 and atomic number 12
Mass number 23 and atomic number 11
Mass number 11 and atomic number 12
questions.explanation: The mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons, so 11 + 12 = 23. The atomic number is the number of protons, which is 11. The 11 electrons balance the 11 protons in this neutral atom.

questions.topic: The rate and extent of chemical change
questions.q: At a school in Leicester, Zara investigates a reaction between two gases in a sealed container. If the pressure is increased while the temperature is kept the same, what happens to the rate of reaction?
options: It increases because the gas particles are closer together and collide more frequently.
It decreases because the gas particles have less room to move.
It increases because each gas particle has more kinetic energy.
It stays the same because pressure does not affect gas concentration.
questions.explanation: Increasing pressure reduces the volume available, so the gas particles are more crowded and collide more often. At constant temperature the average kinetic energy of the particles is unchanged, so the correct reason is the increased frequency of collisions.

questions.q: Which formula is the general formula for alkanes?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
CₙH₂ₙ
CₙH₂ₙ₊₁
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons in which carbon atoms are joined by single bonds. Their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; for example, propane is C₃H₈. CₙH₂ₙ is the general formula for alkenes, not alkanes.

questions.q: Aisha in Cardiff sets up the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate using inert electrodes. Which product is formed at the negative electrode?
options: Sulfur dioxide gas
Hydrogen gas
Copper metal
Oxygen gas
questions.explanation: Positive copper(II) ions are attracted to the negative electrode, where they gain electrons and form copper metal. Oxygen gas is formed at the positive electrode when water is oxidised. Hydrogen can also be produced at the cathode in some aqueous solutions, but copper is deposited in copper(II) sulfate solution.

questions.topic: The rate and extent of chemical change
questions.q: Mei in Nottingham follows the volume of gas produced in a reaction. The volume rises quickly at first, then the curve becomes less steep before becoming horizontal. Which statement best explains why the curve becomes less steep before it levels off?
options: The activation energy increases as products are formed.
The catalyst is gradually used up during the reaction.
The concentration of the reactants falls, so successful collisions happen less often.
The forward reaction has stopped because dynamic equilibrium has been reached.
questions.explanation: As reactants are used up, their concentration decreases, so there are fewer successful collisions per second and the rate slows. A horizontal section usually means the limiting reactant has been used up or the reaction has finished, not that the catalyst has been consumed or the activation energy has changed.

questions.q: In the fractional distillation of crude oil, which fraction is collected nearest the top of the fractionating column?
options: Refinery gases
Kerosene
Bitumen
Diesel oil
questions.explanation: Fractions near the top are made of smaller hydrocarbon molecules with lower boiling points, and refinery gases are the lightest fraction listed. Bitumen, diesel oil and kerosene are collected lower down because their molecules are larger and have higher boiling ranges.

questions.q: A metal is extracted from its oxide by electrolysis in industry because carbon reduction is not suitable. Which metal is it?
options: Aluminium
Iron
Zinc
Copper
questions.explanation: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce aluminium oxide in the same way that iron oxide is reduced in a blast furnace. Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of aluminium oxide dissolved in molten cryolite. Iron, zinc and copper are commonly obtained using reducing agents such as carbon or by other displacement methods.

questions.topic: Atomic structure and the periodic table
questions.q: Which statement describes a typical property of transition metals?
options: They are non-metals with full outer electron shells.
They can form coloured compounds and act as catalysts.
They form only ions with a 1+ charge.
They are all in Group 1 and react vigorously with water.
questions.explanation: Transition metals often form coloured compounds and many are useful catalysts, for example iron in the Haber process. They do not all have one outer electron or a full outer shell, and they commonly form ions with different positive charges.

questions.topic: The rate and extent of chemical change
questions.q: At a school in Manchester, equal volumes of 0.50 mol dm⁻³ and 1.00 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid are added to separate equal lengths of magnesium ribbon, with magnesium in excess, at the same temperature. Compared with the 0.50 mol dm⁻³ acid, what happens with the 1.00 mol dm⁻³ acid?
options: It reacts faster and produces the same volume of hydrogen.
It reacts at the same rate and produces twice the volume of hydrogen.
It reacts faster and produces twice the volume of hydrogen.
It reacts more slowly and produces the same volume of hydrogen.
questions.explanation: The more concentrated acid has more acid particles in the same volume, so collisions with magnesium are more frequent and the reaction is faster. Since the volume of acid is the same and magnesium is in excess, the 1.00 mol dm⁻³ acid supplies twice the number of moles of hydrochloric acid, so it produces twice the number of moles of hydrogen gas, which is twice the volume under the same conditions.

questions.q: Zainab carries out a flame test on a compound. The flame is orange-red. Which metal ion is present in the compound?
options: Na⁺
K⁺
Ca²⁺
Cu²⁺
questions.explanation: Calcium ions give an orange-red flame in a flame test. Sodium ions give a yellow flame, potassium ions give a lilac flame, and copper ions give a green flame.

questions.q: A student in Leicester prepares a paper chromatogram. Why is the start line drawn with pencil rather than with a pen?
options: Pencil graphite reacts with the solvent to produce a gas that pushes the samples upwards.
Pencil graphite is a catalyst that speeds up the movement of the solvent.
Pencil graphite is soluble in water, so it helps the samples dissolve.
Pencil graphite is insoluble in the solvent, so it does not form extra spots.
questions.explanation: The start line must not dissolve and move with the solvent. Pencil graphite is insoluble, so it stays on the paper and does not create extra coloured spots that could be confused with the sample spots.

questions.q: A pupil in Leeds is learning about air pollution. Why is carbon monoxide harmful even at low concentrations?
options: It reacts with ozone in the upper atmosphere and causes acid rain.
It binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells and reduces the amount of oxygen that can be carried around the body.
It dissolves in rainwater to form carbonic acid, making lakes acidic.
It absorbs infrared radiation more strongly than methane and is the main greenhouse gas.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen does, so less oxygen is transported in the blood. It does not form carbonic acid in rainwater; carbon dioxide does that.

questions.q: A garage in Manchester services petrol cars. Which statement explains how nitrogen oxides are formed in a car engine?
options: Nitrogen and oxygen from the air react at the high temperatures inside the engine.
Carbon dioxide is broken down by the spark plug into nitrogen oxides.
Sulfur impurities in petrol react with oxygen to make nitrogen oxides.
Incomplete combustion of petrol produces nitrogen oxides directly from carbon and hydrogen.
questions.explanation: At the high temperatures in a car engine, nitrogen and oxygen from the air can react to form nitrogen oxides. Incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and particulates, not nitrogen oxides directly from carbon and hydrogen.

questions.topic: Bonding, structure and the properties of matter
questions.q: Priya compares magnesium oxide and sodium chloride. Which statement best explains why magnesium oxide has a much higher melting point than sodium chloride?
options: Magnesium oxide has smaller ions, so its covalent bonds are stronger than the ionic bonds in sodium chloride.
Magnesium oxide is a simple molecular compound with stronger intermolecular forces than sodium chloride.
Magnesium oxide has delocalised electrons that hold the ions in place more strongly.
Magnesium and oxide ions have higher charges, so the electrostatic attractions in the lattice are stronger than in sodium chloride.
questions.explanation: Both solids have giant ionic lattices. Magnesium oxide contains Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions, while sodium chloride contains Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, so the higher charges in magnesium oxide produce stronger electrostatic attractions and a higher melting point.

questions.topic: Bonding, structure and the properties of matter
questions.q: A pupil in Cardiff heats a piece of a thermosoftening polymer and reshapes it. Which statement explains why it can be reshaped repeatedly on heating?
options: Covalent bonds within the polymer chains break, allowing the chains to move freely.
The polymer molecules evaporate and condense into a new shape on cooling.
Cross-links between the polymer chains break permanently, so the polymer cannot reharden.
Forces between polymer chains weaken when heated, so the chains can slide over each other.
questions.explanation: In a thermosoftening polymer, the covalent bonds within each chain remain intact. The weaker forces between chains are overcome on heating, allowing the chains to slide and the polymer to be reshaped as it cools and hardens again.

questions.topic: Bonding, structure and the properties of matter
questions.q: During a practical in Swansea, a student hits a crystal of sodium chloride with a hammer and it cracks. Which statement explains why?
options: Layers of ions are shifted, so ions with the same charge line up and repel each other.
The delocalised electrons move away, leaving the lattice unsupported.
Water molecules enter the lattice and dissolve it during the impact.
The strong covalent bonds between molecules are broken by the impact.
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride has a giant ionic lattice. When the crystal is struck, layers of ions can slide; if ions of the same charge line up, they repel and the lattice splits.

questions.q: At a school in Bradford, a student uses these bond energies: C–H = 413 kJ mol⁻¹, O=O = 498 kJ mol⁻¹, C=O = 805 kJ mol⁻¹ and O–H = 464 kJ mol⁻¹. Use the equation CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g). What is the overall energy change for the reaction as written?
options: −818 kJ mol⁻¹
−3466 kJ mol⁻¹
+818 kJ mol⁻¹
−2648 kJ mol⁻¹
questions.explanation: Bonds broken: 4 × 413 + 2 × 498 = 1652 + 996 = 2648 kJ mol⁻¹. Bonds formed: 2 × 805 + 4 × 464 = 1610 + 1856 = 3466 kJ mol⁻¹. Energy change = 2648 − 3466 = −818 kJ mol⁻¹, so the reaction is exothermic.

questions.q: A class in Belfast investigates energy changes. Which process is endothermic?
options: The neutralisation of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide
The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate when heated strongly
The reaction of magnesium with dilute hydrochloric acid
The combustion of methane
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate absorbs energy overall, so it is endothermic. Combustion, neutralisation and the reaction of magnesium with acid all release energy, so they are exothermic.

questions.q: Samir, a student in London, burns ethanol in a spirit burner to heat water in a copper can. The measured energy released per mole is lower than the theoretical value. Which statement best explains this?
options: Some heat is lost to the surroundings, and the ethanol may not burn completely.
The thermometer transfers chemical energy into the water during the experiment.
The water absorbs more energy than the ethanol releases, so the measured value is always negative.
The copper can catalyses the combustion of ethanol, so it lowers the energy released.
questions.explanation: The calculation using the water temperature rise assumes that all the heat released is absorbed by the water. In practice, heat escapes to the surroundings and incomplete combustion can release less energy, so the measured value is usually lower than the theoretical value.

questions.q: A student dissolves 4.50 g of sodium chloride in enough water to make 250 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration of the solution in g dm⁻³?
options: 18.0 g dm⁻³
1.13 g dm⁻³
4.50 g dm⁻³
0.018 g dm⁻³
questions.explanation: The volume is 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³, so concentration = 4.50 g ÷ 0.250 dm³ = 18.0 g dm⁻³. Multiplying 4.50 g by 0.250 instead of dividing gives 1.13 g dm⁻³, which is incorrect.

questions.q: Propane burns completely: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. What mass of carbon dioxide is produced when 0.10 mol of propane burns completely? (Mr of CO₂ = 44)
questions.explanation: The equation shows that 1 mol of propane produces 3 mol of carbon dioxide, so 0.10 mol produces 0.30 mol. The mass is 0.30 mol × 44 g mol⁻¹ = 13.2 g. Using a 1:1 ratio would give 4.4 g, which is incorrect.

questions.q: 25.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sulfuric acid. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. What volume of the sulfuric acid is needed?
options: 25.0 cm³
50.0 cm³
12.5 cm³
100 cm³
questions.explanation: The sodium hydroxide amount is 0.200 mol dm⁻³ × 0.0250 dm³ = 0.00500 mol. The equation shows that 2 mol NaOH react with 1 mol H₂SO₄, so 0.00500 mol NaOH needs 0.00250 mol H₂SO₄. This gives a volume of 0.00250 mol ÷ 0.100 mol dm⁻³ = 0.0250 dm³ = 25.0 cm³.

questions.q: Why can excessive use of nitrate fertilisers on farmland cause a problem in nearby rivers?
options: Nitrates make the river water acidic and dissolve rocks.
Nitrates evaporate from fields and form acid rain.
Nitrates are soluble and can be washed into rivers, causing excessive growth of algae.
Nitrates neutralise oxygen in the river, so fish cannot breathe.
questions.explanation: Nitrate ions are very soluble, so rainwater can wash them from fields into streams and rivers. The extra nitrate encourages excessive growth of algae, and when this decays it can use up oxygen in the water.

questions.q: In the UK, water companies supply potable water. Which statement best explains what potable water is?
options: Water that is safe to drink.
Water that contains no dissolved substances.
Water that has been distilled to remove all microorganisms.
Water with a pH of exactly 7 and no ions.
questions.explanation: Potable water means water that is safe to drink; it can still contain small amounts of dissolved ions. Distilled water contains no dissolved substances, but that is not what potable means.

questions.topic: Atomic structure and the periodic table
questions.q: An atom of calcium-40 has atomic number 20. Which element has atoms with one more proton than an atom of calcium-40?
options: Scandium
Titanium
Argon
Potassium
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the number of protons, so calcium has 20 protons. The element with 21 protons is scandium; potassium has 19 and titanium has 22.

questions.topic: Atomic structure and the periodic table
questions.q: In the alpha-particle scattering experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil, but a small number were deflected. What did this provide evidence for?
options: Atoms are solid spheres that cannot be divided.
Electrons are spread evenly throughout a positive sphere.
The nucleus contains protons, neutrons and electrons.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a small, dense positive nucleus.
questions.explanation: Most alpha particles passing straight through shows that most of the atom is empty space. The small number deflected through large angles shows a small, dense positive nucleus. An evenly spread positive sphere model would not produce such large deflections.

questions.topic: Atomic structure and the periodic table
questions.q: As you go down Group 1, the elements become more reactive. Which statement best explains this trend?
options: The number of outer electrons increases down the group, so more electrons are lost.
The outer electron is in a shell further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.
The atoms have more protons, so the outer electron is lost more easily.
The atoms have full outer shells, so they react by gaining electrons.
questions.explanation: Going down Group 1, the atoms get larger and the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded. This makes the outer electron easier to lose, so reactivity increases.

questions.topic: The rate and extent of chemical change
questions.q: For the equilibrium H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), what is the effect of adding more hydrogen at constant temperature?
options: The value of the equilibrium constant decreases and less hydrogen iodide is formed.
The equilibrium position does not change because there are two moles of gas on each side.
The equilibrium position shifts to the left and less hydrogen iodide is formed.
The equilibrium position shifts to the right and more hydrogen iodide is formed.
questions.explanation: Adding more hydrogen increases the concentration of a reactant. The equilibrium shifts to the right to reduce the change, producing more hydrogen iodide. The equilibrium constant is unchanged because the temperature is unchanged.

questions.q: Kofi in London has a molecule of heptane, which contains 7 carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms are in one molecule of heptane?
questions.explanation: Heptane is an alkane, so it follows the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. With n = 7, the number of hydrogen atoms is 2 × 7 + 2 = 16. A value of 14 would fit an alkene or cycloalkane with seven carbon atoms, not an alkane.

questions.q: A gas fire is used in a flat in Leeds with too little ventilation. Some of the methane burns incompletely. Which gas is produced by incomplete combustion and is dangerous because it reduces the amount of oxygen that red blood cells can carry?
options: Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen
Carbon monoxide
Methane
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion happens when there is insufficient oxygen, producing carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport. Carbon dioxide is mainly formed during complete combustion, so it is not the poisonous gas described.
